description: git-plugin hooks - PR validation, issue auto-close enforcement, merge-method enforcement, and PR-branch drift detection

hooks.prompt: Check the 'body' field in tool_input for GitHub issue closing keywords: closes, fixes, resolves (case-insensitive, followed by #N or owner/repo#N). If the body already contains closing keywords, return {"ok": true}. If the body contains a line starting 'No linked issue:' (case-insensitive) followed by a reason, the author is stating that no issue exists for this PR, so return {"ok": true}; do not judge whether the reason is good enough. If the body references an existing issue without closing it, such as 'Refs #N', 'Part of #N', 'Related to #N' or 'Related: #N' (case-insensitive, also with owner/repo#N), the PR is one part of a larger issue that should stay open, so return {"ok": true}; do not require a closing keyword. If the PR title or body is clearly for infrastructure, documentation, or dependency updates with no bug or feature issue to close, return {"ok": true}. If the title or body describes a bug fix or feature implementation but the body has no closing keywords, no non-closing issue reference, and no 'No linked issue:' line, return {"ok": false, "reason": "PR body is missing issue closing keywords. Add 'Closes #N', 'Fixes #N', or 'Resolves #N' to automatically close the related issue when this PR merges to the default branch. Use 'Fixes' for bugs, 'Closes' for features/enhancements, 'Resolves' for general issues. For multiple issues repeat the keyword: Fixes #1, Fixes #2. If the PR is part of a larger issue it should not close, reference it with 'Refs #N' or 'Part of #N' instead of a closing keyword. If no issue exists for this work, add a line 'No linked issue: <reason>' instead; do not create an issue only to close it."}
